starting_question: Does MurJ enable lipid II to reach the periplasmic leaflet, or cause another peptidoglycan defect?

actual_observations.observation: MTSES specifically inhibited functional MurJ-A29C; periplasmic ColM cleavage declined while lipid-linked label accumulated.
Removing the outer membrane did not restore cleavage; disrupting the inner membrane did.
Flipping persisted after FtsW depletion in a rodA deletion background; residual FtsW remained a stated caveat.
actual_observations.source_locator: Final Results; supplementary Figs. S8–S9 discussed, not independently reanalyzed

annotation_consequence: Supports MurJ-dependent lipid II translocation in vivo. The access control distinguishes substrate sequestration from failed ColM import or activity.
experiment_dependence: Chemical genetics, radiolabel/HPLC, spheroplast access and membrane disruption; all author experiments.
reasoning_reported_vs_reconstructed: Published outcomes were known during selection. Observations are authors’ experiments; the question sequence and compact inference boundaries are retrospective reconstruction. No new biological experiment was performed.
verification_scope: Full main Results, Fig. 1–3 legends and assay rationale inspected. Supplementary raw measurements and purified transport were not reproduced.

gene_protein: FtsW with cognate divisome bPBP; complex members and orthologs grouped
organism: Escherichia coli (2011); Streptococcus thermophilus, Staphylococcus aureus, Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Streptococcus pneumoniae (2019)
starting_question: Is FtsW a lipid II transporter, a polymerase, or an enzyme requiring a spatially compatible partner?

actual_observations.observation: FtsW-containing proteoliposomes increased NBD-lipid-II access to dithionite and labeled vancomycin; lumenal-marker controls argued against simple leakage.
actual_observations.source_locator: Results, Figs. 5–7; leakage control described in main text

actual_observations.observation: Purified FtsW alone lacked detectable polymerization; cognate bPBP addition restored it. FtsW catalytic substitution abolished product despite inactive bPBP transpeptidase retaining stimulation.
Removing the bPBP membrane helix prevented stimulation; helix swaps and compensatory interface substitutions changed activity. Catalytic variants failed cellular complementation.
actual_observations.source_locator: Figs. 1–2; main Results; supplementary findings discussed

annotation_consequence: Assigns partner-dependent peptidoglycan polymerase activity to FtsW. The 2011 access observations remain recorded; 2019 authors explicitly did not formally exclude additional flippase activity.
experiment_dependence: Reconstitution/access assays, purified polymerization, interface perturbations and cellular genetics; all author experiments.
reasoning_reported_vs_reconstructed: Published outcomes were known during selection. Observations are authors’ experiments; the question sequence and compact inference boundaries are retrospective reconstruction. No new biological experiment was performed.
verification_scope: Both papers’ relevant main Results and controls inspected; 2019 purification/polymerization methods read. No independent reproduction or resolution of every assay discrepancy.

gene_protein: DsbD; β membrane domain and α/γ domains grouped
starting_question: Can the two essential membrane-domain cysteines form a disulfide if predicted on opposite membrane faces?

actual_observations.observation: Redox-sensitive alkylation and engineered cleavage supported an intramolecular Cys163–Cys285 disulfide.
Intact spheroplasts protected both cysteines; membrane disruption exposed them, with cytoplasmic and periplasmic controls.
Protease-marked vesicle orientation independently associated cysteine accessibility with the cytoplasmic face.

annotation_consequence: Refines the transmembrane electron-transfer mechanism and rejects the earlier static opposite-face cysteine model. Cytoplasmic accessibility permits a cavity interpretation; the periplasmic γ-domain encounter remained unresolved.
experiment_dependence: Alkylation, site-directed proteolysis, spheroplasts and orientation-resolved vesicles; all author experiments.
reasoning_reported_vs_reconstructed: Published outcomes were known during selection. Observations are authors’ experiments; the question sequence and compact inference boundaries are retrospective reconstruction. No new biological experiment was performed.
verification_scope: Full relevant Methods, Results, Figs. 1–5 legends and Discussion read. Neither a complete dynamic transport cycle nor current topology prediction was reproduced.

gene_protein: CcdA versus DsbD; donor/acceptor partners treated as one specificity investigation
starting_question: Does membrane-core homology confer the same periplasmic acceptor range as multidomain DsbD?

actual_observations.observation: Reciprocal complementation restored cytochrome-c-related functions; CcdA rescue required TrxB and CcmG/HelX.
CcdA did not reduce DsbC or DsbD-γ, including when DsbD accessory domains were coexpressed.
actual_observations.source_locator: Fig. 2B–C; Roles of α and γ Results

annotation_consequence: Supports a transmembrane reducing pathway shared with DsbD while restricting demonstrated acceptor scope. Exported partners and appended domains cannot be assumed functionally interchangeable.
experiment_dependence: Heterologous complementation, heme staining, growth/oxidase assays and thiol-redox measurements; all author experiments.
reasoning_reported_vs_reconstructed: Published outcomes were known during selection. Observations are authors’ experiments; the question sequence and compact inference boundaries are retrospective reconstruction. No new biological experiment was performed.
verification_scope: Main Results and Discussion plus relevant assay methods read. Direct CcdA–HelX chemistry and all homolog functions were inferred, not established by these assays.

gene_protein: TrxA/thioredoxin 1, experimentally exported variants; DsbB partner
starting_question: Does relocating a cytoplasmic reductant change its cellular reaction direction?

actual_observations.observation: Signal-sequence fusions showed processing, export-reporter activity, oxidized thioredoxin and partial dsbA rescue. Fractionation alone was inconclusive.
actual_observations.source_locator: Results: Export of thioredoxin; Fig. 2–3; Tables 2–3

actual_observations.observation: Pulse-chase OmpA oxidation accelerated with exported TrxA. Reconstructed genotypes established DsbB dependence, correcting the 1998 strain error; a DsbB–TrxA mixed disulfide was trapped.
actual_observations.source_locator: Fig. 1–2; Table 2; Mechanism of oxidation Results

actual_observations.observation: Higher exported-TrxA expression reduced alkaline-phosphatase recovery; authors proposed saturation of reoxidation capacity.

annotation_consequence: Demonstrates conditional oxidant activity after engineered relocation, dependent on partner access and abundance. It does not annotate native TrxA as a naturally exported oxidant.
experiment_dependence: Engineered targeting, export reporters, complementation, redox trapping and pulse-chase; all author experiments.
reasoning_reported_vs_reconstructed: Published outcomes were known during selection. Observations are authors’ experiments; the question sequence and compact inference boundaries are retrospective reconstruction. No new biological experiment was performed.
verification_scope: Both papers’ relevant full Results and correction read. The oxidation-versus-reduction explanation at high expression remains an interpretation of the reported readouts.

gene_protein: AmiC and AmiA amidases; AmiB comparison grouped
starting_question: Which export and targeting features place active amidases where cell separation occurs?

actual_observations.observation: Functional GFP fusions complemented chaining; Tat loss blocked processing and peripheral localization. Spheroplast release supported periplasmic export.

AmiC accumulated at constrictions; N-terminal targeting fragments localized without catalytic regions. An exported catalytic-region-containing deletion lacked septal concentration yet suppressed chaining when induced.
AmiB-GFP suppressed Tat-mutant chaining but its degradation prevented reliable localization.

annotation_consequence: Supports Tat-dependent export and separable AmiC septal targeting. Targeting, export and catalysis are distinct properties; overexpression rescue does not establish that septal concentration is essential.
experiment_dependence: Functional fusions, microscopy, export processing/release and deletion constructs; all author experiments.
reasoning_reported_vs_reconstructed: Published outcomes were known during selection. Observations are authors’ experiments; the question sequence and compact inference boundaries are retrospective reconstruction. No new biological experiment was performed.
verification_scope: Relevant full Results, fusion-function controls and localization Discussion read. No direct binding target or reason for Tat preference established.
cross_lane_link: Root causal-role investigation examines EnvC/NlpD-mediated amidase activation; not repeated here.
